Hi Emma / Solace procurement team —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we covered and proposed next steps so nothing gets lost: 

Call highlights (from our side):
- Solace is evaluating Redwood for real-time document summarization in two products (CareNote and IntakeFlow).
- Primary procurement consideration: internal finance prefers a Purchase Order (PO) cadence but the procurement team is open to marketplace purchase if it preserves existing vendor workflows and billing entity.
- Compliance: SOC2 + standard security addenda are required; customer data will remain in your AWS account for Private Deployment evaluation.

Open questions / asks from Solace:
1) If we go AWS Marketplace, can you accept a Private Offer (POA) so the billing goes through your Azure-native procurement system? (I know phrasing is a bit tangled; we discussed billing entity and contract flow.)
2) Lead time for PO creation and payment terms (Net 30/45/60) — procurement to confirm.
3) Procurement contact and purchase flow (person + email) — so we can route the SOW/PO correctly.

What Redwood will do next:
- Share an initial SOW and an AWS Marketplace checklist (what we need for Private Offer submission). Attached SOW-draft-v1.pdf and AWS-Marketplace-PO-checklist.xlsx.
- Karthik will follow up with a short note explaining differences between Marketplace private offers vs. standard PO (billing/legal flow).
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up with procurement and finance to lock the path (PO vs marketplace).

Proposed next steps:
- Emma / procurement: confirm preferred path (Marketplace private offer vs. standard PO/card) and provide procurement contact by EOD Friday 4/21.
- Redwood: send final SOW and marketplace checklist by EOD 4/18.

If anything above misses a nuance, flag it and I’ll update.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

— Jordan

Thanks Jordan — nice summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) High-level preference: procurement would prefer a Marketplace route if Redwood can publish a Private Offer that maps to our billing/legal entity (Solace Health, Inc.). The primary driver is our vendor governance and the desire to keep vendor billing on the marketplace ledger.
2) If Private Offer isn’t available in time, we can process a traditional PO (our default fall-back). For card purchases, volume and SSO integration make it less attractive for enterprise licensing.
3) Lead times: procurement estimates ~2–3 weeks to issue a PO once terms and an SOW are agreed; if we can do Marketplace Private Offer, that often shortens internal approvals but can add 3–5 business days for listing setup on the vendor side.

I’m copying procurement@solacehealth.com to provide our procurement contact and an expected PO timeline PDF.

We’ll review the SOW you sent and get back with comments by EOD Thursday (4/20).

Best,

Hi Emma — thanks for the context, a few practical notes from procurement/enablement that should help the internal decision: 

Marketplace (AWS Private Offer) pros/cons:
- Pros: matches Solace billing cadence (vendor billed via AWS), often speeds internal approvals since procurement systems already trust marketplace listings, supports private pricing and term attachments (SOW or customer-specific PO).
- Cons: requires Redwood to create the Private Offer and coordinate listing metadata (billing entity, VAT/tax info). There’s a short operational checklist (we attached it in the first email) — key fields we’ll need: billing entity name, registered address, and the Redwood SKU or publisher account we’ll link.

Standard PO flow pros/cons:
- Pros: straightforward for vendors who are set up in Solace AP; no marketplace setup required.
- Cons: longer approval chain for new vendors, separate invoicing and reconciliation for Solace AP team.

What we need from Solace procurement to move either path: 
1) Procurement contact name + email (to receive SOW and invoice contact).
2) Confirmation of preferred billing entity and billing address.
3) A target payment term (Net 30/45/60).
4) Any required contract clauses or redlines (if legal will be in the loop, please share the standard vendor addendum).

If Solace wants the AWS Marketplace Private Offer path, we can start assembling the private offer package today; timeline for Redwood to submit is ~2 business days once we have the billing entity and SOW signature. If you prefer PO, plan for 10–15 business days on your side for a new vendor in AP.

I’ll coordinate with our enablement team to prepare the Private Offer payload and share the DocuSign if needed.

Thanks — Karthik
